 How to follow Mexico City Grand Prix on the BBC 
 Image source, Getty Images Image caption, The Mexico City Grand Prix signed a contract extension last year to stay on the F1 calendar until 2028
 By Sophie Trifonoff BBC Sport journalist Published 26 October 2026 
 Updated 31 October 2026 Lewis Hamilton will start on pole position for the first time as a Ferrari driver at the Mexico City Grand Prix, which takes place on Sunday, 1 November. 
 The seven-time world champion beat Mercedes' George Russell by 0.009 seconds as the two drivers who can potentially stop Kimi Antonelli clinching the title on Sunday locked out the front row.
 Antonelli qualified fifth behind Ferrari's Charles Leclerc and Red Bull's Max Verstappen, but will start fourth because of a one-place penalty for the Dutchman.
 The only way Antonelli can be prevented from winning the title is if Russell wins and the Italian finishes lower than ninth, or if Hamilton wins and Antonelli is out of the points.
 Lights out for Sunday's 71-lap race is at 20:00 GMT.

 Session start times and BBC coverage 
 Commentary of the weekend will be available across BBC Radio 5 Live, Radio 5 Sports Extra, BBC Sounds and the BBC Sport website and app.
 You can also ask your smart speaker to "play 5 Live", for example.
 Make sure to listen to every episode of the Chequered Flag podcast. For the first time this year, the post-race show for every grand prix is available to watch on BBC iPlayer and YouTube. , external 
 All times GMT 
 Sunday, 1 November 
 Race: 20:00 - BBC Radio 5 Live 
 Image source, Getty Images Image caption, World champion Lando Norris took a dominant win in Mexico City last year, with Charles Leclerc and Max Verstappen also on the podium
 What is the Mexico City weather forecast? 
 The forecast suggests it will be a warm race day in the Mexican capital. 
 For Sunday's race, which starts at 2pm local time, conditions will be sunny with a gentle breeze and a top temperature of 24C.
